propositions: A check's PASS result is indistinguishable from the check never having run when an absence assertion (not in, assert not, == "", empty-collection) is derived from subprocess/file/network/captured output with no producer-liveness verification (exit status, non-empty capture, asserted presence).

A check's FAIL result is equally unreliable when a presence assertion misinterprets instrument failure or empty input as a catastrophic condition (e.g., git show receiving bogus paths due to word-splitting failure reports total loss where none occurred).

The fail-open oracle antipattern includes absence-only greps (grep -c "^FAILED", ! grep -q "FAIL") with no producer-liveness check, silent lookup/membership miss paths (continue on KNOWN_ENV_HELPERS miss), and pgrep patterns that can self-match the matching process.

The fail-open language must be added to existing code-review criteria (tests for test-oracle population, error-handling for shipped-code population) rather than creating a new criterion; calibration must validate that the pattern language fires reliably from both hosts on nine pre-fix instances and is silent on nine corresponding post-fix instances.

The code-review author guide (rebar explain review) must document the fail-open pattern with at least two worked examples demonstrating detection and remediation (producer-liveness assertion before trusting any absence derived from the producer).

Calibration replay must record per-case findings with quoted claims naming the seeded fail-open defect for all pre-fix cases, verify zero findings on post-fix cases (with fallback protocol for unrelated fires), and measure false-positive posture against standing no-fire families.
